{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Of the {{sc|Annotations}}, vvhy they vvere made, & vvhat matter they cōteine.}}Now, though the text thus truely tran{{ls}}lated, might {{ls}}ufficiently, in the {{ls}}ight of the learned and al indifferent men, both controule the aduer{{ls}}aries corruptions, and proue that the holy Scripture vvhereof they haue made {{ls}}o great vauntes, make nothing for their nevv opinions, but vvholy for the Catholike Churches beleefe and doctrine, in all the pointes of difference betvvixt vs: yet knovving that the good and {{ls}}imple may ea{{ls}}ily be {{ls}}educed by {{ls}}ome fevv ob{{ls}}tinate per{{ls}}ons of perdition (whom vve {{ls}}ee giuen ouer into a reprobat {{ls}}en{{ls}}e, to whom the Go{{ls}}pel, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2 Cor. 2.''}}vvhich in it {{ls}}elf is the odour of life to {{ls}}aluation, is made the odour of death to damnation, ouer vvho{{ls}}e eies for {{ls}}inne & di{{ls}}obedience God {{ls}}uffereth a veile or couer to lie, whiles they read the nevv Te{{ls}}tam{{+-|e|n}}t, euen as the Apo{{ls}}tle {{ls}}aith the Ievves haue til this day, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2 Cor. 3.''}}in reading of the old, that as the one {{ls}}ort can not finde Chri{{ls}}t in the Scriptures, reade they neuer {{ls}}o much, {{ls}}o the other can not finde the Catholike Church nor her doctrine there neither) and finding by experience this {{ls}}aying of S.
